newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on frosty weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on frosty weather concerns.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on the potential for frost to hit portions of the U.S. Midwest by late September, traders said.
"It's weather, that's the talk on the floor. Fund buying, weather and technical buying," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Private forecasters early Thursday were hinting at potential freezing temperatures by late September.
A cold front could bring freezing temperatures from Kansas City to Chicago by September 24, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express Inc.

He said U.S. forecasting models indicated a cold front would move into the corn belt on September 21, bringing very cold temperatures. He put the freeze line from Kansas City to Chicago by September 24.

But gains in corn were limited by Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for normal to above normal temperatures and above normal rainfall in the Midwest from September 17 through September 21.
Corn closed two to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 4-1/2 at $3.65-1/4.
Tenco Inc bought five million bushels of December and Rosenthal Collins bought four million December, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, down from 86,727 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Prudential Securities sold 450 December $3.80 calls at two cents, Refco Inc bought 400 March $3.40 calls at 16-3/4 and LFG Futures sold 300 December $3.00 puts at 2-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, down from 28,435 Wednesday.
